lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: The Company’s largest customer accounted for 18%, 19% and 20% of consolidated net sales for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
No other customers account for more than 10% of consolidated net sales for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, or 2023.
During the year ended December 31, 2025, our top five customers accounted for approximately 38% of our consolidated net sales, with one customer accounting for 18% of consolidated net sales.
In fiscal 2025, our three largest independent distributors generated approximately 32% of our consolidated net sales with the largest accounting for 18% of consolidated net sales.
Historically, we have been able to successfully source materials and consequently are not dependent on a single source for any significant raw material or component.
Our business also depends upon general economic conditions and other market factors beyond our control, and we serve customers in cyclical industries.
Our ongoing success depends on our ability to continue to meet our customers' changing specifications with respect to these criteria.
We rely on independent distributors and independent sales representatives.
We depend on approximately 1,000 independent sales representatives within North America, and approximately 65 third-party warehouses to distribute our products.
We also rely on unpatented proprietary technology and trade secrets.
Our manufacturing processes depend on third parties for raw materials, in particular bronze, iron, brass, stainless steel, carbon steel, zinc, and engineered plastics.
In addition to suppliers, we also rely on third party shippers to assist in transportation of our product throughout the supply chain.
Our ongoing success depends on our ability to recruit, retain and develop highly skilled management and key personnel, as well as our ability to effectively manage human capital resources.

The ultimate impact of an infectious disease outbreak on our business depends on the severity, location and duration of outbreaks, and the actions of government and health officials in response to the outbreaks, none of which is predictable at this time.

Our ability to generate sufficient cash flow from operations to make scheduled payments on our debt will depend on a range of economic, competitive and business factors, many of which are outside our control.
The funded status of the defined benefit pension plans depends on such factors as asset returns, market interest rates, legislative changes and funding regulations.

In addition, our business depends on the strong brand reputation we have developed; if this reputation is damaged as a result of litigation or product liability claims, it may be difficult to maintain our pricing positions and market share with respect to our products.
Our primary sources of liquidity are available cash and cash equivalents, cash flow from operations, and borrowing availability under our $200.0 million revolving credit facility.

As part of our global sourcing strategy, we have entered into agreements with key suppliers that require the supplier to maintain minimum levels of inventory to support certain products for which we require a short lead time to fulfill customer demand.

Lease payments included in the measurement of the lease liabilities are comprised of fixed payments, variable payments that depend on an index or rate, and amounts probable to be paid if an option is reasonably certain to be exercised.
